description: Guidance on minimizing development customizations during implementation projects
best_practices: Avoid development customizations as much as possible to reduce risks, shorten timelines, and minimize maintenance costs
Design changes can impact requirements, and requirement changes can impact time needed for technical resources
Evaluate out-of-the-box capabilities before building custom solutions
Document any unavoidable customizations with clear business justification
common_mistakes: Building custom solutions when standard platform features would suffice
Not accounting for the maintenance cost of customizations over time
Making design changes without evaluating downstream impact on requirements and timelines
checklist: Review out-of-the-box features before designing customizations
Document business justification for any custom development
Assess maintenance cost and upgrade impact of each customization
tips: Customizations create long-term maintenance burden and can break during platform upgrades
success_criteria: Customization count is minimized and each one has documented justification
Standard platform features are used wherever they meet requirements

description: Establishing clear project roles, responsibilities, and governance from day one
best_practices: Agree from the beginning what project roles and responsibilities are
Define how the implementation will be conducted
Identify procedures for escalating project risks and problems
Decide on communication methods and frequency early in the project
Establish the function of the Architect role: governs changes to the data model and coordinates various logic pieces such as triggers, scheduled jobs, and technical design
common_mistakes: Not defining escalation procedures before problems arise
Unclear ownership of data model governance
No designated architect to coordinate cross-cutting technical decisions
checklist: Define all project roles and document responsibilities
Create escalation procedures document
Establish communication cadence and channels
Assign architect role for data model and technical design governance
Document decision-making authority for technical and business choices
tips: The architect role is critical for coordinating triggers, scheduled jobs, and technical design decisions across the project
success_criteria: All team members understand their roles and responsibilities
Escalation paths are documented and tested
Technical decisions flow through the designated architect

description: Planning for documentation requirements including compliance and regulatory needs
best_practices: Discuss documentation processes and requirements upfront
Request compliance documentation at the launch of a project to ensure you meet local industry regulations and standards
Account for the fact that some companies require heavy amounts of documentation to meet compliance regulations
common_mistakes: Discovering compliance documentation requirements late in the project
Not budgeting time for regulatory documentation
Assuming documentation requirements are the same across regions
checklist: Identify all compliance and regulatory documentation requirements
Determine documentation standards and templates
Request existing compliance documentation from the customer
Build documentation effort into the project timeline
tips: Life sciences implementations often have stricter documentation requirements than other industries due to regulatory compliance
success_criteria: All regulatory documentation requirements are identified before development begins
Documentation processes are agreed upon by all parties

description: Aligning implementation timelines with platform release schedules and holidays
best_practices: Consider the platform release schedule and holidays while planning the implementation timeline
Decide on object naming and documentation standards before building anything
Plan ahead to conduct integration tests well before client UAT
Allow sufficient time between integration testing and UAT to resolve challenges
common_mistakes: Performing integration testing too close to UAT, leaving insufficient time to resolve issues
Not accounting for platform release windows that may affect sandbox or production environments
Starting development without agreed naming conventions
checklist: Map implementation timeline against platform release schedule
Identify holiday periods that may affect team availability
Schedule integration testing with buffer time before UAT
Agree on naming conventions and documentation standards before development starts
tips: Integration tests should involve both the mobile app and web interfaces
Increase API limits during regression and UAT to avoid governor limit issues during testing
success_criteria: Timeline accounts for platform release windows and holidays
Integration testing completes with buffer time before UAT begins

description: Best practices for performance testing and device consistency during implementation
best_practices: Conduct performance tests from within the customer network on a representative's machine from the start for the best real-world experience
Maintain device consistency during unit, regression, and UAT testing phases
Consider bandwidth, outdated browser versions, and network latency impacts on user experience
Validate with tests before every code deployment
Consider validation of all tests upon every push of code to a development branch
common_mistakes: Testing with a Mac and Chrome during regression, then switching to Windows and Chrome for UAT
Doing regression testing with one iPad version and UAT with a different iPad version
Not testing from the actual customer network environment
Discovering performance issues only at go-live because tests were run in optimal conditions
checklist: Define target devices and browsers for all testing phases
Ensure device consistency across regression, UAT, and production testing
Set up performance testing from within the customer's actual network
Create test validation gate for every code deployment
Document minimum bandwidth and browser version requirements
tips: Behavior and test criteria will differ across different devices, browsers, and OS versions, so keep testing environments consistent
Do not wait until go-live to discover network latency issues
success_criteria: All testing phases use consistent devices and browser versions
Performance tests are run from real customer network conditions
No surprises on go-live day due to untested environments

description: Standards for naming and organizing custom fields on platform objects
best_practices: Always implement the API naming convention agreed upon at the onset of the project
Keep field naming universal by adding either a prefix or suffix of the organization to distinguish between platform standard custom fields and customer-built custom fields
Identify in the description section: group that requested the field, ISO codes of the countries, business units, and integrations using the field
Organize deprecated fields by prefixing labels with 'dep_[fieldname]'
common_mistakes: Not establishing naming conventions before development begins
Mixing platform-delivered custom fields with customer-created fields without clear distinction
Not documenting field purpose and requesting team in the description
Leaving deprecated fields cluttering the field list
checklist: Define and document API naming convention before development
Choose prefix or suffix strategy for distinguishing field origins
Create field description template including: requesting group, ISO codes, business units, integrations
Implement 'dep_' prefix convention for deprecated fields
tips: Examples of naming: 'OneEducation_<client>__c' or 'License_<client>__c'
The platform sorts fields by label name, so prefixing deprecated fields with 'dep_' moves them to the bottom of the list, making the environment easier to manage
success_criteria: All fields follow the agreed naming convention
Every custom field has a complete description documenting its purpose and consumers

description: Understanding and planning around platform field and object limitations
best_practices: Understand field limitations per object before design begins
Plan for field allocation across current and future needs
Track field usage to avoid hitting limits mid-project
common_mistakes: Not accounting for field limits in the initial data model design
Hitting field limits mid-implementation and needing to redesign
checklist: Review field limits: 800 custom fields per object
Review external ID limits per object
Review rollup summary field limit: 25 per object
Review master-detail relationship limit: 2 per object
Review total relationship field limit: 40 per object (master-detail plus lookup combined)
tips: Document current field counts per object at the start of the project to plan allocation
success_criteria: Field usage stays well within platform limits
Data model design accounts for future expansion within limit constraints

description: Best practices for managing profiles, page layouts, and field-level security
best_practices: Keep the number of profiles to a minimum
Rename unused profiles to include 'dep_' prefix to organize them
Use field-level security to hide fields from users instead of page layouts for compliance
Minimize the number of page layouts to decrease the likelihood of inconsistencies for different record types
Consider using Dynamic Forms for ease of maintenance as an alternative to many page layouts
Evaluate very carefully before adding security exclusions to bypass user access permissions in triggers
common_mistakes: Using page layouts to restrict field access instead of field-level security, which leaves data visible in reports
Creating too many profiles and page layouts leading to maintenance burden and inconsistencies
Bypassing user permission enforcement in triggers without understanding audit implications
Not recognizing that the CRM is a point-in-time system and audits can lead to inaccurate assessments if permissions are bypassed
checklist: Audit existing profiles and consolidate where possible
Implement field-level security for all compliance-sensitive fields
Document justification for any permission bypass in trigger code
Evaluate Dynamic Forms as an alternative to multiple page layouts
Ensure page layout count is minimized per record type
tips: Page layouts prevent users from seeing fields on the form, but do NOT prevent them from seeing data in reports. Only field-level security provides complete access restriction.
Dynamic Forms can significantly reduce the number of page layouts needed
success_criteria: Field-level security is used for all compliance-restricted fields
Profile count is minimized and documented
No unauthorized permission bypasses exist in trigger code

description: Best practices for migrating data into the platform safely and efficiently
best_practices: Create unique external ID fields on objects to move data between environments, since the 18-character record ID is system-generated and unique only within the org
Take extra care to protect data integrity of the production environment since the platform does not have a database rollback feature during data loads
Review trigger handler documentation and understand the purpose of each trigger handler before data migration
Consider using an integration user with the 'SkipTriggerHandlers' permission to bypass all trigger handlers during data migration for better performance
Alternatively, disable handlers selectively from the admin console for a more targeted approach
common_mistakes: Using record IDs to move data between environments (they are org-specific)
Keeping all trigger handlers enabled during data migration, causing slow performance or governor limit issues
Not having a rollback plan since the platform lacks database rollback during data loads
Not running post-migration jobs after disabling trigger handlers
checklist: Create external ID fields on all migrated objects
Document data migration rollback strategy
Review all trigger handlers and determine which to disable during migration
Choose trigger bypass strategy: integration user permission vs. admin console selective disable
Plan post-migration job execution for all disabled handlers
Validate data integrity after migration completes
tips: Using an integration user to bypass triggers only affects that user; other users still have handlers enforced. This is suitable for systems with live users.
Selectively disabling handlers from the admin console affects all users. This is more suitable for systems without live users.
success_criteria: Data migrates without hitting governor limits
All post-migration jobs run successfully
Data integrity is validated after migration

topic: Trigger Handler Bypass During Data Loads
description: Detailed guidance on which trigger handlers can be safely disabled during data migration and the equivalent jobs to run afterward
best_practices: Identify handlers that have equivalent batch jobs that can be run post-migration
Run the equivalent batch jobs immediately after data loads complete
For historical data loads, consider disabling additional lock handlers and validation handlers
common_mistakes: Disabling handlers without running equivalent post-load jobs
Not re-enabling handlers after data migration completes
Forgetting to disable lock handlers for historical data loads
checklist: Disable sample limit initialization handlers during account data loads; run 'Assign Sample Limit Templates to Accounts' job afterward
Disable contact point handlers (email, phone, social) during data loads; run 'Search Before Create Jobs' afterward
Disable healthcare provider handler during data loads; run 'Search Before Create Jobs' afterward
Disable NPI and specialty handlers during data loads; run corresponding jobs afterward
Disable visit changed event handlers during data loads; run 'Visit Share Management Jobs' and 'Provider Account Territory Information Job' afterward

For historical data loads: consider disabling lock handlers (visit, document, expense, disbursement), validation handlers (time-off, holiday, conflict, business hours), and workflow permission handlers
tips: Maintain a checklist of disabled handlers and their corresponding post-load jobs to ensure nothing is missed
Lock handlers prevent modifications to records in submitted or signed states, so disabling them is appropriate for historical data but risky for live systems
success_criteria: All disabled handlers have their post-load equivalent jobs executed
All handlers are re-enabled after migration
Data integrity is maintained for locked and submitted records

description: Best practices for configuring territory models and hierarchies
best_practices: Understand territory limitations: up to 1000 territories are allowed out-of-the-box
If the org will be expanded to new business units or countries, understand what platform limitations will affect the expansion
Build the territory hierarchy before building the role hierarchy since the role hierarchy needs to mirror the territory hierarchy
Ensure users are always assigned to a territory; they will have limited access to the application without one
common_mistakes: Building the role hierarchy before the territory hierarchy, leading to mismatches
Assigning one territory to multiple users (avoid this)
Not requesting territory limit extensions before hitting the 1000-territory cap
Leaving users unassigned to territories, causing access issues
checklist: Assess total territory count needed and request extensions if over 1000
Build territory hierarchy first
Build role hierarchy to mirror territory hierarchy
Verify all users are assigned to at least one territory
Confirm no territory is assigned to multiple users
Plan for future business unit or country expansion within territory limits
tips: Territory limit extensions are available by request but will affect system performance
Users can be assigned to multiple territories, but do NOT assign one territory to multiple users
success_criteria: Territory hierarchy is built before role hierarchy
All users have territory assignments
Territory count is within limits or extensions are approved

topic: Account Tab and App Version Management
description: Using the correct account interface and keeping mobile app versions current
best_practices: Always use the custom Accounts tab shipped with the life sciences app instead of the standard platform Accounts tab
Keep mobile OS version and app version up to date
Review the certified and supported devices and OS versions published every release
common_mistakes: Using the standard platform Accounts tab, which causes Search Before Create to not work
Running outdated mobile app or OS versions
Not checking certified device lists for each release
checklist: Configure users to use the custom Accounts tab
Verify mobile app and OS are on supported versions
Review certified device list for each platform release
tips: The Search Before Create feature only works on the custom Accounts tab, not the standard one
success_criteria: All users access accounts through the custom tab
Mobile devices are on certified and supported versions

description: Optimizing entity schema configuration for mobile sync performance
best_practices: Each new entity schema record means more time required to sync; deactivate records not needed for mobile push using the Active flag
For each entity schema record, ensure the 'Permitted Profiles' field is configured with ONLY required profiles
Apply filter criteria to account-related object schema records to ensure downloading only records for accounts present on the device
Enable attachments only for schema records of objects that require attachment downloads on mobile
All entity schema settings must have a 'where' clause to limit records returned
Remove access to objects and fields that the user does not need functionally, especially long text area fields
common_mistakes: Leaving all entity schema records active when many are not needed for mobile
Not applying filter criteria, causing excessive data download
Enabling attachments for all objects instead of only those that need them
Missing 'where' clauses on schema records, leading to full table downloads
Including unnecessary long text area fields that slow sync
checklist: Audit all entity schema records and deactivate unnecessary ones
Configure 'Permitted Profiles' for each active schema record
Add territory-based filter criteria to account-related schema records
Verify attachment enablement is limited to required objects
Ensure every schema record has a 'where' clause
Remove access to unnecessary objects and long text area fields
tips: Use territory-based filtering: 'ParentId IN (SELECT AccountId FROM ProviderAcctTerritoryInfo WHERE IsAvailableOffline = true AND Territory2.Name = '{USER.TERRITORY}')' pattern for account-related objects
Update attachment schema where clause to limit by parent type and recent modification dates to avoid exceeding 100K records
success_criteria: Sync times are acceptable for end users
Only required data is downloaded to devices
No unnecessary objects or fields are included in sync

description: Recommendations for targeting the right volume of accounts for mobile sync
best_practices: Target accounts for mobile use by adding appropriate filter conditions to entity schemas
Limit to either 5000 accounts with 3 months of related activity OR under 3000 accounts with up to 6 months of related activity
Use the IsAvailableOffline field on territory info records to define which accounts are available for the mobile app
Create a custom process to set IsAvailableOffline to false for accounts not needed on mobile
common_mistakes: Syncing all accounts to mobile devices without filtering
Not using the IsAvailableOffline flag to control mobile account scope
Exceeding recommended account volumes, causing slow sync times
checklist: Define account volume target (under 5000 with 3 months activity or under 3000 with 6 months)
Implement IsAvailableOffline flag management process
Apply territory-based filter to the Account entity schema
Test sync times with the target account volume
tips: By default, when a territory info record is created, IsAvailableOffline is set to true. Build a process to manage this proactively.
Make sure you use the SOQL where clause provided in the out-of-the-box entity schema for Account
success_criteria: Account count on devices stays within recommended limits
Sync times are acceptable for field users
IsAvailableOffline is actively managed

description: How to monitor sync transactions and handle errors effectively
best_practices: Monitor the sync transactions queue in the admin console every day
Check if there are transactions stuck in 'New' status for more than a day
Check the 'Ready to Process' flag and related fields: Missing Items, Excess Items, Pending
When transactions error out, analyze each error individually
Fix the issue and retry the transaction from the admin console
common_mistakes: Not monitoring sync transactions daily
Ignoring stuck transactions in 'New' status
Not analyzing individual sync errors to find root causes
Leaving errored transactions unresolved, causing dependent transactions to stay in 'Waiting' status
checklist: Set up daily monitoring of sync transaction queue
Define alert threshold for transactions in 'New' status (recommend: more than 1 day)
Check 'Ready to Process' flag status
If Ready to Process is NO: check Missing Items, Excess Items, and Pending flags
For stuck transactions: contact the user and request a full manual sync
Analyze and resolve errored transactions promptly
tips: Until errored transactions are successfully processed or cancelled, any dependent transactions will stay in 'Waiting' status
If a user's transactions stay in 'New' for a long time, have them perform a full manual sync by tapping the gear icon and tapping 'Sync Database'
Monitor the sync queue the same way you would monitor any other ETL job
success_criteria: Sync transactions are monitored daily
Stuck or errored transactions are resolved within 24 hours
No long-running chains of waiting transactions

description: Understanding and resolving common sync transaction errors
best_practices: Categorize sync errors to identify patterns and systemic issues
Address root causes rather than just retrying failed transactions
common_mistakes: Retrying transactions without fixing the underlying cause
Not recognizing patterns in sync errors that indicate systemic issues
checklist: Check for record locking issues
Check for timeout errors
Check for heap size exceptions
Check for CPU time limit exceptions
Check for governor limit violations from high load or non-bulkified code
Check for validation rule conflicts
Check for database-level rules that do not match UI logic
Check for field-level uniqueness or non-null constraint violations
Check for trigger, flow, workflow, or process builder failures causing insert/update failures
tips: Governor limit issues during sync often indicate non-bulkified code or high-load scenarios
Validation rules and database constraints that differ from UI logic are a common source of sync errors
success_criteria: Sync error root causes are identified and resolved
Error patterns are tracked and systemic issues are addressed

description: Recommended values for mobile sync configuration settings
best_practices: Configure sync settings based on recommended values and adjust based on customer needs
Set Number of Items per Transaction to 10 (note: this includes the transaction itself, so 10 means 9 transaction items)
Set Mobile Non-WiFi Data Limit to 25 MB
Set Mobile Timeout Period to 60 minutes (reduce if more frequent PIN entry is needed)
Set Number of Retry Attempts to 3
Enable 'Optimize performance by grouping Items' to reduce SOQL queries
Enable 'Cancel sync for deleted records' to auto-cancel transactions deleting already-deleted records
Enable 'Cancel sync when record isn't found' to auto-cancel transactions for missing records
Enable 'Retry sync for locked rows' to auto-retry on lock row errors
common_mistakes: Setting items per transaction too high (max is 25, but 10 is recommended)
Not enabling the grouping optimization, leading to excessive SOQL queries
Not enabling auto-cancel for deleted records, causing unnecessary retry cycles
checklist: Set Number of Items per Transaction: 10
Set Mobile Non-WiFi Data Limit: 25 MB
Set Mobile Timeout Period: 60 minutes
Set Number of Retry Attempts: 3
Enable Optimize performance by grouping Items: true
Enable Cancel sync for deleted records: true
Enable Cancel sync when record isn't found: true
Enable Retry sync for locked rows: true
tips: The items per transaction field includes the transaction itself. So entering 9 means 8 transaction items will be included.
The maximum items per transaction is 25. Even if you enter more, the system caps at 25 (24 items + 1 transaction).
Grouping items by operation and entity type reduces SOQL queries by processing items with the same order value as a single batch
success_criteria: All sync settings match recommended values or have documented justification for deviation
Auto-cancel and retry mechanisms are enabled

topic: Sharing Settings and Trigger Performance for Sync
description: Optimizing sharing settings and triggers for mobile sync performance
best_practices: In org-wide defaults, sharing settings for objects synced regularly from mobile to the platform should be Private instead of Public
For objects being synced to mobile, avoid long-running queries in triggers
Use platform events for post-trigger calculations and functions instead of inline processing
common_mistakes: Setting sharing to Public Read Only for synced objects, which slows queries
Having complex, long-running queries in triggers for synced objects
Performing all post-trigger work inline instead of using platform events
checklist: Review sharing settings for all synced objects
Set synced objects to Private sharing where possible
Audit trigger queries on synced objects for performance
Refactor long-running trigger logic to use platform events
tips: Private sharing helps queries run faster and completes sync quicker than Public sharing
Out-of-the-box options are available for configuring platform events for post-trigger processing
success_criteria: Synced objects use Private sharing settings
No long-running trigger queries exist on synced objects
Platform events are used for post-trigger async processing

description: Considerations for building components that work offline in mobile runtime
best_practices: Understand the impact of offline mode on the lightning mobile runtime
Ensure components use base components that are supported for offline rendering
Fetch data through supported wire adapters only
Verify entities are supported through the UI API for offline use
common_mistakes: Using unsupported base components in offline-capable LWCs
Using unsupported wire adapters for data fetching
Not verifying UI API support for entities used offline
checklist: Review supported base components for offline rendering
Verify all wire adapters used are supported for offline
Check entity UI API support for any custom objects used offline
Test component behavior in offline mode on real devices
tips: Base component support, wire adapter support, and UI API entity support are the three critical compatibility checks for offline LWCs
success_criteria: All offline LWCs use supported base components and wire adapters
Offline functionality is validated on real devices

description: Web browser session management and environment separation
best_practices: Work in separate browser contexts when accessing multiple platform environments such as sandboxes or production instances
Use different Chrome Users/People, Firefox Profiles, or browser extensions that create separate contexts
Understand that all incognito/private windows share a common set of cookies
common_mistakes: Accessing multiple environments from the same browser context, causing cookie and session cross-contamination
Using multiple incognito windows for different org logins (they share cookies)
Not recognizing that session corruption can affect platform functionality
checklist: Use separate browser profiles for each environment
Educate team on incognito window cookie sharing limitation
Document browser context requirements for the team
tips: An incognito window can separate from a non-incognito window, but multiple incognito windows for multiple org logins can cross cookies
Chrome Users/People feature is the most reliable way to maintain separate browser contexts
success_criteria: No session cross-contamination issues during development
All team members use separate browser contexts per environment

description: Best practices for query optimization, code quality, and safe deployments
best_practices: Follow SOQL best practices for query optimization
Follow Apex code best practices
Validate with tests before every code deployment
Consider validation of all tests upon every push of code to a development branch
common_mistakes: Not validating tests before deployment, leading to go-live surprises
Writing non-optimized SOQL queries that hit governor limits
Deploying code without running the full test suite
checklist: Review SOQL queries for optimization
Follow Apex code best practices
Run all tests before every code deployment
Automate test validation on every push to dev branch
tips: Consistent test validation on every code push prevents surprises on go-live day
success_criteria: All code deployments pass test validation
SOQL queries are optimized and within governor limits

description: Understanding indexes, skinny tables, and query optimization thresholds
best_practices: Ensure proper indexes and external IDs exist for fields used in 'where' clauses to make queries faster
Understand index selectivity thresholds to ensure indexes are useful
Consider skinny tables for high-volume objects
Plan for data archiving in the initial design
Use report filters, pre-aggregate data, de-normalize data, or use a data warehouse for reporting
common_mistakes: Not creating indexes for frequently queried fields
Not understanding that indexes must be below selectivity thresholds to be useful
Using NOT or != operators which will not use indexes
Not planning for data archiving from the start
checklist: Create custom indexes for fields in where clauses: threshold is lower of (10% of first 1M + 5% over 1M) or 333,333 records
Standard indexes threshold: lower of (30% of first 1M + 15% over 1M) or 1M records
AND conditions: below 20% of total records or 666K for custom index
OR conditions: below 10% of total records or 333K in summation of all indexes
Avoid predicates that won't use indexes: != (not equal to) and NOT IN
Evaluate skinny tables for high-volume objects (requires platform support to enable)
Design archiving strategy as part of initial data model
tips: Skinny tables provide better cache utilization, reduced joins, and are invisible to end users. They support reports, list views, and SOQL queries.
Data archiving should be considered in the initial design, not as an afterthought
success_criteria: All frequently queried fields have appropriate indexes
Index selectivity is within required thresholds
Archiving strategy is documented and planned

description: Guidelines for API integration design and performance
best_practices: Avoid Apex triggers or workflows firing on API REST reads and inserts
Choose the fastest operation available: Insert is fastest, then Update, then Upsert
Keep record sizes within the 3 MB limit
Optimize sharing models for API performance (use fewer sharing models)
common_mistakes: Triggering expensive Apex logic on API operations
Using Upsert when Insert would suffice
Not monitoring record sizes in API operations
Complex sharing models degrading API performance
checklist: Review triggers and workflows that fire on API operations
Choose optimal operation type for each integration
Verify record sizes are under 3 MB
Evaluate sharing model complexity and simplify where possible
tips: Operation speed ranking: Insert (fastest) > Update > Upsert
Simpler sharing models lead to better API performance
success_criteria: API integrations use the fastest viable operation type
No unnecessary triggers fire on API operations
Record sizes stay within limits

description: Guidelines for configuring sharing rules and security models
best_practices: Follow a pattern of least-privilege access
Avoid over-protection that adds unnecessary complexity
Do not nest groups deeply
common_mistakes: Over-protecting with unnecessarily complex sharing rules
Creating deeply nested groups that degrade performance
Not following least-privilege principle
checklist: Audit sharing rules for unnecessary complexity
Verify group nesting depth is minimal
Confirm least-privilege access pattern is followed
Document sharing model decisions and justifications
tips: Deeply nested groups cause performance degradation. Keep the hierarchy as flat as possible.
success_criteria: Sharing model follows least-privilege principle
Group nesting is minimal
No unnecessary sharing rule complexity

description: Handling custom translations for page layout section headers
best_practices: Avoid using standard section headers in layouts; always use custom sections
Standard section headers cannot be custom translated; they auto-translate based on user language settings
If custom translation is needed, hide the standard section header and create a new custom section header
Custom section headers can be translated using the Translation Workbench
common_mistakes: Relying on standard section headers when custom translations are needed
Not realizing standard section translations are not configurable via Translation Workbench
Mixing standard and custom section headers inconsistently
checklist: Use custom section headers for all layouts requiring translated headers
Configure translations via Translation Workbench for custom sections
Verify translations render correctly for all target languages
tips: Standard section headers auto-translate based on user language and are NOT configurable. Always use custom sections if you need custom translations.
success_criteria: All page layout section headers that need custom translations use custom sections
Translations are verified across all supported languages

description: Planning and executing integration testing and user acceptance testing
best_practices: Plan integration tests well before client UAT to allow time for issue resolution
Integration tests should cover both mobile app and web interfaces
Increase API limits during regression and UAT to avoid governor limit issues
Raise support cases early for any questions that need platform support answers
common_mistakes: Scheduling integration testing too close to UAT
Only testing one interface (web or mobile) during integration testing
Not increasing API limits for test phases, causing false failures
Waiting too long to raise support cases for blocking questions
checklist: Schedule integration testing with sufficient buffer before UAT
Include both mobile and web interfaces in integration test scope
Request API limit increases for regression and UAT phases
Identify and raise support cases for any blocking questions early
tips: Integration testing challenges discovered too close to UAT create project risk and timeline pressure
success_criteria: Integration testing completes with time to resolve issues before UAT
Both mobile and web interfaces are validated
No governor limit failures during testing due to API limits

topic: Trigger Handlers Reference for Data Loads
description: Reference catalog of handlers with equivalent post-load jobs that can be safely disabled during migration
best_practices: Use this reference to identify which handlers to disable during data loads
Always run the equivalent job after re-enabling or after completing data loads
common_mistakes: Disabling handlers without knowing which post-load job to run
Forgetting to run post-load jobs for handlers that maintain denormalized data
checklist: Account sample limit handlers: run 'Assign Sample Limit Templates to Accounts' job post-load
Contact point email handler: run 'Search Before Create Jobs' post-load
Contact point phone handler: run 'Search Before Create Jobs' post-load
Contact point social handler: run 'Search Before Create Jobs' post-load
Healthcare provider handler: run 'Search Before Create Jobs' post-load
Healthcare provider NPI handler: run 'Search Before Create Jobs' post-load
Healthcare provider specialty handler: run 'Search Before Create Jobs' post-load
Visit changed event share handler: run 'Visit Share Management Jobs' post-load
Visit changed event territory handler: run 'Provider Account Territory Information Job' post-load
tips: These handlers maintain denormalized data (email IDs, phone numbers, social identifiers, specialties, NPI) on healthcare provider records. The corresponding jobs recalculate this data after bulk loads.
success_criteria: All handler/job pairs are tracked and executed
Denormalized data is accurate after migration completes

description: Additional handlers to consider disabling for historical data loads beyond the standard data migration handlers
best_practices: For historical data loads, evaluate disabling additional categories of handlers beyond the standard migration set
Disable workflow permission handlers to allow historical records through without stage-path validation
Disable content document lock handlers for loading historical attached documents
Disable visit lock handlers for loading historical visit records in various states
Disable scheduling validation handlers for loading historical visits that may conflict with time-off or holidays
common_mistakes: Not recognizing that historical data may violate current business rules (e.g., visits on holidays, conflicting schedules)
Applying current validation rules to historical data that was valid at the time it was created
Forgetting that lock handlers prevent modifications to submitted or signed records
checklist: Review stage path permission handlers for workflow states in historical data
Review document lock handlers if loading historical document links
Review visit lock handlers if loading historical visits in submitted/signed states
Review scheduling validation handlers (time-off, holiday, conflict, business hours, future limit)
Review expense and disbursement lock handlers for historical financial records
Re-enable all handlers after historical data load completes
tips: Historical data loads require a different handler disable strategy than ongoing data migration because the data may not conform to current business rules
Lock handlers are the most commonly needed disablements for historical loads since submitted/signed records cannot be modified otherwise
success_criteria: Historical data loads complete without validation or lock errors
All handlers are re-enabled after load
Data integrity is maintained for both historical and current records
